records.title: Aluminium
records.summary: The reference material: most spacecraft hulls are aluminium. Against galactic cosmic rays, heavy nuclei break up in aluminium into lighter fragments and neutrons, so thick aluminium gives limited extra protection.

data.notes: The reference material: most spacecraft hulls are aluminium. Against galactic cosmic rays, heavy nuclei break up in aluminium into lighter fragments and neutrons, so thick aluminium gives limited extra protection.

records.title: Polyethylene (HDPE)
records.summary: Hydrogen-rich plastics are among the most effective practical shields per kilogram, because hydrogen nuclei break up incoming heavy ions with few secondary particles. Polyethylene panels have been added around ISS sleeping quarters.

data.notes: Hydrogen-rich plastics are among the most effective practical shields per kilogram, because hydrogen nuclei break up incoming heavy ions with few secondary particles. Polyethylene panels have been added around ISS sleeping quarters.

records.title: Water
records.summary: Dual-use: crew already carry tonnes of water. Water walls and stowage around sleep areas and storm shelters add protection at no extra launch mass.

data.notes: Dual-use: crew already carry tonnes of water. Water walls and stowage around sleep areas and storm shelters add protection at no extra launch mass.

records.title: Liquid hydrogen
records.summary: Pure hydrogen is the best shield per unit mass, but its very low density, need for cryogenic storage and boil-off make it impractical as a habitat shield.

data.notes: Pure hydrogen is the best shield per unit mass, but its very low density, need for cryogenic storage and boil-off make it impractical as a habitat shield.

records.title: Lithium hydride
records.summary: High hydrogen content and low mass, but it reacts with water and needs to be sealed. Studied for reactor and deep-space shielding.

data.notes: High hydrogen content and low mass, but it reacts with water and needs to be sealed. Studied for reactor and deep-space shielding.

records.title: Lunar regolith (soil)
records.summary: Free, local mass. Bury the habitat or build berms and sandbags. A metre or more cuts dose substantially, though heavy oxygen and silicon nuclei produce some secondary neutrons.
tags: GCR: Similar to Al per mass

data.notes: Free, local mass. Bury the habitat or build berms and sandbags. A metre or more cuts dose substantially, though heavy oxygen and silicon nuclei produce some secondary neutrons.

records.title: Mars regolith
records.summary: Like lunar regolith, but Mars also has a thin atmosphere (about 20 g/cm² overhead at Gale crater) that already halves the cruise dose. Subsurface ice adds hydrogen.
tags: GCR: Similar to Al per mass

data.notes: Like lunar regolith, but Mars also has a thin atmosphere (about 20 g/cm² overhead at Gale crater) that already halves the cruise dose. Subsurface ice adds hydrogen.

records.title: Lead
records.summary: Excellent for X-rays and gamma rays on Earth, but a poor space shield: heavy nuclei fragment and produce secondary neutrons. Very heavy to launch.

data.notes: Excellent for X-rays and gamma rays on Earth, but a poor space shield: heavy nuclei fragment and produce secondary neutrons. Very heavy to launch.

records.title: Tantalum / tungsten
records.summary: High-Z metals are used as thin spot shields around sensitive electronics, not around crew.

data.notes: High-Z metals are used as thin spot shields around sensitive electronics, not around crew.

records.title: Boron nitride nanotubes (hydrogenated)
records.summary: Boron-10 captures secondary neutrons, and the nanotubes can store hydrogen. Strong enough to be structural.

data.notes: Boron-10 captures secondary neutrons, and the nanotubes can store hydrogen. Strong enough to be structural.

records.title: Carbon-fibre composites
records.summary: Lower atomic number than aluminium, giving fewer heavy fragments. Can replace some aluminium structure.

data.notes: Lower atomic number than aluminium, giving fewer heavy fragments. Can replace some aluminium structure.

records.title: Food and supplies
records.summary: Orion's solar-storm plan has the crew build a shelter in the central stowage area, surrounded by stored supplies.

data.notes: Orion's solar-storm plan has the crew build a shelter in the central stowage area, surrounded by stored supplies.

records.title: The human body
records.summary: Deep organs such as blood-forming bone marrow are partly shielded by the rest of the body. Dosimeters on the skin overestimate dose to deep organs.

data.notes: Deep organs such as blood-forming bone marrow are partly shielded by the rest of the body. Dosimeters on the skin overestimate dose to deep organs.

records.title: Wearable vest (e.g. AstroRad)
records.summary: Shields organs most sensitive to radiation, such as bone marrow, ovaries and lungs. Flew on Artemis I on one mannequin (MATROSHKA AstroRad Radiation Experiment).

data.notes: Shields organs most sensitive to radiation, such as bone marrow, ovaries and lungs. Flew on Artemis I on one mannequin (MATROSHKA AstroRad Radiation Experiment).

records.title: Active magnetic or electrostatic shields
records.summary: Superconducting magnets or charged structures could deflect particles, like Earth's magnetic field. Not yet feasible at the needed scale and power.

data.notes: Superconducting magnets or charged structures could deflect particles, like Earth's magnetic field. Not yet feasible at the needed scale and power.

records.title: Earth's atmosphere + magnetic field
records.summary: About 1000 g/cm² of air plus the magnetic field. ISS is above the air but still largely inside the magnetic field, which is why its dose is much lower than in deep space.
